gloss: still far from enough, not yet by a long shot

definitions.gloss: still far from enough, not nearly there yet
definitions.explanation: Emphasizes that something is far from reaching a goal, standard, or completion. Stronger than まだ alone.

definitions.gloss: still more to come, there is much more ahead
definitions.explanation: Indicates that something will continue or that there is still plenty remaining.

examples.english: I still have a long way to go.

examples.japanese: {日本語|にほんご}はまだまだ{上手|じょうず}じゃない。
examples.english: My Japanese is still far from good.

examples.japanese: {練習|れんしゅう}が{足|た}りない。まだまだ{努力|どりょく}しないといけない。
examples.english: I haven't practiced enough. I still need to work much harder.

examples.japanese: {夏|なつ}はまだまだ{続|つづ}く。
{時間|じかん}はまだまだある。
examples.english: There is still plenty of time.

examples.japanese: この{先|さき}まだまだ{面白|おもしろ}くなるから、{楽|たの}しみにしていてね。
examples.english: It's going to get much more interesting from here, so look forward to it.

notes:
まだまだ is the reduplicated form of まだ (still, not yet), adding emphasis to mean "far from enough" or "still a long way to go."

COMMON PATTERNS:
- まだまだです: I still have a long way to go (humble response to praise)
- まだまだ{足|た}りない: still far from enough
- まだまだこれから: the best is still to come
- まだまだ{続|つづ}く: far from over

USAGE:
まだまだです is one of the most common humble responses when receiving a compliment in Japanese. It conveys modesty by saying one is far from accomplished.
- Sense 1 (not enough) often carries a tone of self-reflection or humility
- Sense 2 (more to come) is more neutral or encouraging, indicating that something will continue or has further to go

SIMILAR WORDS:
まだ simply means "still" or "not yet." まだまだ emphasizes that the gap is large.
